# Barq (برق): PlanetBlindTech's tashkeel engine

A fast Arabic diacritizer in C++ (word lexicon, word bigrams and small decision trees), written by Shamseddin of PlanetBlindTech and included in Fasih with his agreement; fine-tuned for Fasih by Riad Assoum, under the GNU GPL v3 or later.

- `cpp/`: the engine's source, as Shamseddin sent it, with one change for Fasih: on Windows the model path is converted from UTF-8 to UTF-16 and opened with `CreateFileW`, so folders with non-ASCII names (an Arabic Windows user name) work.
- `python/`: his training pipeline.
- `bin/tashkeel_engine.dll`: 64-bit Windows build, cross-compiled with zig: `python3 -m ziglang c++ -target x86_64-windows-gnu -O3 -std=c++17 -shared -DTASHKEEL_EXPORTS -D_LIBCPP_ENABLE_CXX17_REMOVED_FEATURES -Icpp/include cpp/src/diacritizer.cpp cpp/src/c_api.cpp -o bin/tashkeel_engine.dll`
- `models/tashkeel_engine.tash`: the model Fasih ships, retrained with `python/train_pipeline.py --max-vocab 600000 --max-bigrams 1200000 --max-tree-lines 600000 --max-tree-samples 1000000 --oov-trees 40 --irab-trees 40 --morph-trees 32 --max-depth 7` on a balanced 9.5 million sentence mix: QCRI's diacritized Arabic Wikipedia (343,781 sentences, four times; Mohamed and Mubarak, Advancing Arabic Diacritization, EMNLP 2025, github.com/qcri/advancing-arabic-diacritization), TigreGotico's Arabic diacritized text (twice), ArVoice's text, about 1 million sentences from Shamela (ReligiousLLMs), 1.2 million from Abdou's Arabic tashkeel dataset (MIT) and 0.6 million from Tashkeela, with every sentence of the test sets (including WikiNews 2014) removed and hamzat al-wasl written without a vowel throughout.
